key_insight: The paper introduces two Lean 4 benchmarks for quantum algorithms and quantum information, showing that current AI theorem-proving agents improve when given a verified domain library.
engineering_relevance: For quantum software and formal methods teams, the benchmarks provide a reproducible way to measure proof-agent reliability, difficulty, and cost-efficiency on domain-specific verification tasks.
method: Created Lean-QuantumAlg-Bench with 36 theorem-completion tasks and Lean-QIT-Bench with 40 tasks.
Evaluated four models under two settings: task-only baseline and library-augmented deduction (LAD).
Used deterministic proof checking plus targeted semantic review, with difficulty weights assigned before model execution.
evidence_signal: Across eight model-benchmark comparisons, LAD improved both weighted score and completion rate, with top scores reaching 60.4/100 on quantum algorithms and 59.6/100 on quantum information.
watch_item: Results depend on a fixed Lean environment and benchmark-specific libraries, so real-world performance may differ when proofs require broader theory coverage or less controlled tooling.
paper_title: Benchmarking Agents for Proving Theorems in Quantum Algorithms and Quantum Information
